summary: The implementation faithfully realizes the APPROVED design and meets the acceptance criteria. The front-end adds a first-class sbf-solana-solana target (Os.Tag.solana + Abi.solana mirroring .sb0 with the three documented overrides: ELF object format, sbpfv3 default CPU, compiler_rt off), the sbf arch alias, the sbpfv1/2/3 CPU models, isSolana, canDynamicLink gated on os==.solana, and forced self-hosted-linker routing (use_lld=false/use_new_linker=true) — all verified by the freshly built `sig targets` listing solana in both os/abi lists plus sbpfv1/2/3. The self-hosted linker (Elf2.sig) accepts EM_BPF via the EhdrMachine enum + MachineRelocType union with a correct .BPF arm at every exhaustive machine switch (many beyond the design's list, found by build-until-clean), implements the PC2-measured R_SBF reloc values (64_64=1/64_ABS64=2/64_32=10, REL form, lddw low32->slot1/high32->slot2) and the SIMD-0189 relocation-free ET_DYN layout via finalizeBpfSolanaObject, with the rodata-pointer rebase driven from recorded .sbf_lddw relocation sites (not an opcode scan) and guarded. Static syscalls lower per SIMD-0178 to `call imm` (opcode 0x85, src reg 0) with imm=murmur3_32(name,0) and no relocation, via inline asm in FuncGen.sig; compiler_rt/soft-float is defaulted off for solana. I independently confirmed: plain `sig build` compiles clean (4/4, every Elf2 exhaustive switch) and its test step passes; the committed syscalls_demo.so byte-matches the SIMD-0189 contract exactly (ELFCLASS64/LE/ET_DYN/EM_BPF 247/e_phoff=64/e_shoff=0/phnum=2/PT_LOAD PF_R@0 + PF_X@0x100000000) and contains both static-syscall immediates (sol_log_=0x207559bd, sol_sha256=0x11f49d86) with no reloc; and the recorded validator evidence shows the trivial program deploying and EXECUTING on solana-test-validator (err: None, success, rc=0) and the demo's sol_log_ executing on-chain. The dependency-cycle that earlier FEATs cited as blocking `-Denable-llvm` is in fact fixed (the build now reaches discover:llvm); the remaining local LLVM build failure is only LLVM-22 toolchain discovery/compiler_rt.lib on this Windows host, and the LLVM-backed path is proven via the vendored-prefix sigrepro.exe artifact and the CI gate (ci/test-sbpf-solana-target.sh wired into release.yaml with byte-level assertions). Doc (SBPF_SOLANA_TARGET.md), driver (build-sbpf.ps1), CHANGELOG/README, and the 0.6.1 patch bump are all present. No HIGH or MEDIUM issues; three NITs below.

findings.detail: Stale internal contradiction in the recorded evidence: FEAT-002/003/004 state that `sig build -Denable-llvm` is blocked by a 'dependency cycle detected' and could not run, but FEAT-005 fixed that cycle (the idempotent addDep in tools/sig_build/main.sig) and built the LLVM-backed compiler. I verified the cycle is resolved — the build now progresses past the runner to discover:llvm. The earlier findings should be annotated as superseded by FEAT-005 so a future reader doesn't believe the LLVM path is still cycle-blocked. No code change required.

The compiler_rt unit test re-derives the expression `(true and os.tag != .solana)` inline instead of exercising the real want_compiler_rt resolution in Compilation.sig, so it would still pass if that resolution logic later diverged. Consider asserting against the actual Compilation path (or a shared helper) so the test guards the real default rather than a copy of the expression. The behavior itself is independently covered by the CI gate and the byte-verified .so (no soft-float symbols), so impact is low.

The branch bundles build-system changes (idempotent addDep edge dedup, ZigLLVM C++ wrapper wiring in the registered subprocess compile path, extra Windows COM/shell system libs in appendLlvmLinkerArgs) that the FEAT findings describe as pre-existing defects separable from the sBPF feature. They are correct and necessary to produce the LLVM-linked compiler on Windows, but mixing bootstrap/build-runner changes into a feature branch widens the blast radius (AGENTS.md flags build/bootstrap files as sensitive). Prefer landing these as a separate, clearly-scoped commit/PR so a build-graph regression can be bisected independently of the target work. Non-blocking since the plain `sig build` + test step confirm no runner regression.
